subject: Real-world tokens/sec & p95/p99 checkpoint — throughput challenge
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine T. <elaine.t@acme-inc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Real-world tokens/sec & p95/p99 checkpoint — throughput challenge

Hi Elaine,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the Acme inference workload. Per our call, summary and proposed next steps below so we have a tight, repeatable A/B test to compare Redwood against the hyperscaler baseline you shared.

Quick summary of what we heard you need:
- Target workload: product-search autocomplete (prompt len ~40 tokens, response len ~80 tokens average)
- Traffic profile: spiky 200 rps peak, sustained 40 rps baseline; 95th/99th latency SLOs: <= 150ms / <= 350ms
- Quality constraint: match existing accuracy threshold (BLEU-style internal metric) — you said a 1-2% tolerance is acceptable
- Must measure: p95/p99 generation latency (server-side), tokens/sec (aggregate and per-request), and end-to-end 95th latency including network hop for hosted run

Proposed A/B plan (short):
1) Narrow bench: 15-min steady-state runs at 40 rps to validate per-instance tokens/sec and p95/p99.
2) Spike test: ramp to 200rps for 5 minutes to validate autoscaling and tail latency behavior.
3) Real-world replay: replay a 10-min production traffic trace you shared (we'll run both Redwood-hosted and hyperscaler-provided endpoint).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Today (by EOD PT): I’ll drop our test config and a short checklist (attached) so your infra team can validate access.
- Wed 10/20: narrow bench runs (both vendors) — we’ll run in parallel and exchange raw CSV logs.
- Thu 10/21: spike test + replay; Friday 10/22: summary p95/p99 sheet and recommended model/quantization profile.

Questions / asks for your team:
- Please confirm which model variants you want included in the baseline (exact model name + replica size).
- Share the signed NDA/POC terms (if not already) so we can push keys to your VPC test harness.

Attachments: throughput-config.yaml (initial config), canary-run-checklist.md

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the runs and tag Marissa / Dev for infra ops.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[sig]
From: Elaine T. <elaine.t@acme-inc.com>

Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Real-world tokens/sec & p95/p99 checkpoint — throughput challenge

Thanks Sofia — helpful recap. Quick answers:
- Baseline model: hypercloud/small-gen-3 (4x16GB replicates) and their "prod-fast" config you saw in the deck.
- We can run the signed POC today; legal already approved the standard SOW (I’ll forward).
- Our infra contact (owns the replay trace) is Michael R. (included) — he’ll coordinate endpoint access and share the trace.

One thing to flag: our execs care most about the p99 tail under spike because that’s where current infra drops sessions. If Redwood can demonstrate >20% improvement on p99 during a 200rps spike, that will move the deal forward.

We can commit to the Wed narrow run window (10/20, 10:00-13:00 PT). Please confirm the exact run start time so we can reserve the test VPC.

— Elaine
Elaine T.
Director, Search & Relevance | Acme Inc
From: Michael R. <michael.r@hypercloud.ai>
To: Elaine T. <elaine.t@acme-inc.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Real-world tokens/sec & p95/p99 checkpoint — throughput challenge

Appreciate the invite — I’ll stand up the baseline endpoints for hypercloud/small-gen-3 and share instance-level logs. A few technical clarifications from our side so the comparisons are apples-to-apples: 

1) Tokenization parity: please confirm whether you’ll use our tokenizer or canonical BPE; mismatched tokenization changes tokens/sec and p95 calculations.
2) KV-cache warmup: confirm if you’ll start runs with cold caches or pre-warmed KV caches; this materially affects p95 at short run windows.
3) Measurement endpoints: we’ll publish per-request timestamps (server-received, generation-start, generation-end) as CSV. Please publish the same granularity.

Sofia — can you confirm the config details we should expect in throughput-config.yaml? If you share the exact env vars and concurrency settings, we’ll mirror them on our side.

I’ll be available tomorrow AM to coordinate access.

— Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer | HyperCloud Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael R. <michael.r@hypercloud.ai>, Elaine T. <elaine.t@acme-inc.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Real-world tokens/sec & p95/p99 checkpoint — throughput challenge

Quick ops update from Redwood infra before the Wed run (and a couple of clarifications we agreed on internal sync):

- Tokenization: we’ll use the canonical BPE tokenizer (config attached in throughput-config.yaml), and we’ll share the tokenized prompt map so you can validate parity.
- Cache policy: narrow bench will use pre-warmed caches (10-min warmup) to measure steady-state tokens/sec; spike tests will be run from cold start to show tail behavior.
- Concurrency: per-instance concurrency set to 8, batching enabled with max_batch_size=64 and target_batch_latency_ms=10.
- Metrics published: server_received_ts, gen_start_ts, gen_end_ts, token_count, instance_id, cpu/gpu_util. All CSV logs will be uploaded to the shared Drive link (drive.redwood.ai/ACME/throughput-run-logs).

Checklist for tomorrow (10/20, 10:00 PT start):
- Acme: confirm baseline model instance details and provide replay trace ACLs by 09:00 PT.
- HyperCloud: confirm you’ll mirror the BPE tokenizer and publish CSV headers exactly as above.
- Redwood: we will run narrow bench first, then run parallel spike test at 11:30 PT.

Attachments: p95_p99_expected_matrix.xlsx (expected thresholds)

If everyone confirms, we’ll go ahead and schedule the runs. Happy to jump on a 15-min standup 9:15 PT tomorrow if that helps.

— Marissa
Staff SRE (Bench Ops) | Redwood Inference
